newsitem.title: USA: Kmart says expects same-store sales to rise.
newsitem.headline: Kmart says expects same-store sales to rise.

text.p: Kmart Corp Chief Executive Floyd Hall said Wednesday that he expected the company's same-store sales to rise between three percent and 3.5 percent in the 1996 holiday season over the same period a year ago.
Hall, with reporters at the ribbon cutting for Kmart's first New York City store, said the company did not intend to go out on a limb.
"We're looking for a three to 3.5 percent range on comparable stores. Somewhere in there is realistic," he said.

Warren Flick, Kmart's president and general merchandising manager in the United States, said that 1996 full-year earnings per share would be between $0.40 and $0.45, which he said was in line with the Wall Street consensus.
Hall, who said there are plans to open another Kmart in New York City next month, said that sales for September had been disappointing.

"There are people saying there are signs in the last week or so that the economy is starting to soften up," he said. "Some of the September sales numbers were disappointing to some of the analysts. Ours were to us. I don't know if that is indicative of a scenario we will see in the fourth quarter."
He said Kmart was budgeting conservatively and not buying a lot of excess inventory.
"We certainly don't want to come out of this month with a soft growth pattern and big inventory," Hall said.
